text:
Maya: Heads up — saw a sustained p99 latency increase for private VPC tenants after 00:30 UTC. Affected models: opt-2.7b-quant, batching SLOs hit hard.
Ben: saw alerts too, trying to correlate with Dedicated pools. Any NAT/GW churn? :thinking_face: 
Maya: tcp retransmits and tail qlen spikes on the NAT nodes. Packet drops around egress interface.
Alice: can you paste the perf profile from the runtime? wondering if kernel selector fell back to slow path during the spike.
Maya: here are tail lines from the runtime CPU sampling around the window:
```
# sampling summary
20% kv-cache lock contention
15% batch-assemble wait
30% kernel_fallback_dispatch()
10% net: skb_queue_len growth on eth0
```
Carlos: tagging @infra-bot to check NAT path metrics and conntrack counts.
infra-bot: NAT-node-7: conntrack=286k/65536, conntrack_failures=132, tx_queue_len=192, ifconfig eth0 mtu=1500
Ben: conntrack near capacity — we should see conntrack evictions. That can cause retransmits and stall new flows.
Alice: also noticed kernel selector logged fallbacks when sequence > 1024 tokens — maybe due to batching heuristics mispredicting kernel choice under high concurrency.
Maya: repro steps I ran: small load generator hitting private endpoint with 80 concurrent clients and 64-token seq. p50 ~30ms, p99 ~420ms during normal. During incident p99 ~1.8s.
Carlos: running iperf between app plane and NAT node shows intermittent 400-600ms spikes, small bandwidth drop. suspect egress packet shaping or bufferbloat.
Ben: can someone run `conntrack -L | wc -l` and `ss -s` on the NAT nodes? Also paste `sysctl net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max`.
Maya: outputs:
```
$ conntrack -L | wc -l
285932
$ sysctl net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max
net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max = 262144
$ ss -s
TCP: inuse 45000 orphan 0 tw 1200 alloc 50000
```
Alice: conntrack max too low for private env — we should increase to 524288 for these pools, and enable automatic GC tuning.
Carlos: firewall logs show bursts of SYN retransmits from backend GPU hosts to external model vaults (artifact fetches). Those flows were long-lived due to retries and kept conntrack entries.
Ben: That would pollute the table and cause new inference requests to stall while conntrack allocs occur.
Maya: Quick mitigation: add an iptables rule to drop/reject repeated outbound retries to artifact hosts older than X secs? Alternatively tune conntrack timeouts for SYN_RECV->30s.
Alice: also found runtime metrics: kv-cache hit rate dropped from 92% to 64% during spike — maybe because many long-lived artifact fetch flows pushed runtime threads to kernel fallback path and delayed cache locking.
Carlos: plan: 1) increase conntrack_max on NAT nodes, 2) reduce conntrack timeouts for established idle flows, 3) add a short-term iptables-mangle to limit outbound retry rate, 4) instrument kernel selector to emit fallback reasons to tracing.
Ben: agree. I'll roll conntrack_max and timeout change to canary NAT nodes now, then measure.
Maya: doing a canary load now against NAT-node-7 after conntrack bump. p99 dropped to ~540ms, retransmits decreased.
Alice: great. For longer term we should: a) add runtime backpressure on artifact fetches (circuit-breaker), b) adjust batching heuristics to be less aggressive on token sequences >512 when conntrack pressure detected, c) add an eBPF probe on NAT to tag and evict artifact-related flows.
Carlos: opening infra issue to track the NAT kernel tuning + firewall rule: https://redwood.internal/infra/issues/4672 (will add runbook).
Maya: reassigning to Ben for immediate NAT changes, Alice for runtime fixes, Carlos for infra runbook.
Ben: will follow up with deploy logs. :thumbsup:
Alice: I'll add a short trace flag to kernel_selector to force the optimized kernel for a subset of requests so we can A/B compare.
Carlos: Thanks everyone — will monitor overnight and push the eBPF probe draft tomorrow.
Maya: closing thread for now, re-open if p99 climbs again. :white_check_mark:
